title: Versant’s Fandango, Transmit partner on live sports advertising
article_text:
- Transmit and Fandango have partnered to introduce new advertising opportunities during live sports and entertainment programming.

- The partnership allows advertisers to sponsor key moments during live matches without adding traditional commercial breaks.

- The technology is being used during Bundesliga soccer matches streamed free on Fandango in the United States.

Versant’s Fandango-branded streaming platform has partnered with advertising technology company Transmit to introduce new sponsorship opportunities during live sporting events without adding traditional commercial breaks, the companies announced on Thursday.

The technology is being used during Bundesliga soccer matches streamed on Fandango in the United States, allowing advertisers to place sponsorship messages around significant moments during live competition, Versant said in a statement.

Rather than relying on scheduled advertising breaks, Transmit’s technology identifies events such as substitutions, momentum changes, official reviews and other moments when audience engagement may increase. Advertisers can then place sponsorship messages alongside the live programming without interrupting the game itself.

The partnership is being introduced as Fandango expands its sports programming, including coverage of Germany’s Bundesliga soccer league: Under the league’s U.S. distribution arrangement, USA Sports will carry more than 300 Bundesliga matches during the 2026-27 season. At least 30 matches will air on USA Network, while the remaining games will stream free on Fandango.

“The opportunity in streaming isn’t simply to replicate the traditional television model online. It’s to create entirely new experiences for fans, advertisers, and content partners,” Versant President of Digital Platforms and Ventures Will McIntosh said in a statement.

Transmit CEO Seth Hittman said the technology is intended to identify advertising opportunities as they develop during live events, rather than requiring sponsors to rely on predetermined commercial inventory.

“Everyone understands the value of a FIFA World Cup hydration break,” Hittman said. “It’s one of the most effective sponsorship moments in sports because it’s part of the experience, not an interruption to it. We’re taking that same philosophy and applying it dynamically across live sports. Instead of creating value according to a schedule, we’re identifying it in real time.”

The companies said the approach could generate additional advertising revenue from streaming sports while limiting interruptions to viewers.

Versant was spun out of Comcast’s NBC Universal earlier this year, comprising the company’s former cable networks business (except Bravo, which NBC Universal retained) and digital platforms like Fandango. The company also owns a multicast business called Free TV Networks.

Earlier in the week, Versant said it earned $1.59 billion in overall revenue during the third quarter (Q3) of the year, including $373 million in advertising revenue, down 5.3 percent compared to last year on a carve-out basis.

title: Zoox doubles down on F1 presence with Las Vegas GP deal
article_text:
Zoox, the autonomous ride-hailing company, has increased its visibility in motor racing’s elite Formula 1 (F1) after securing a new partnership with the Las Vegas Grand Prix ahead of this year’s edition.

The multi-year partnership sees Zoox, a subsidiary of e-commerce giant Amazon, become the event and official autonomous ride-hail partner of the race, with Zoox gaining brand visibility between Turns 15 and 16, on the F1 rooftop LED, along the Paddock Club escalator, and across the Sphere Experience.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

From the 2027 edition, the company plans to offer rides in its purpose-built robotaxi to and from a dedicated pickup and drop-off zone at Grand Prix Plaza.

The new agreement comes ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas GP race weekend, which is scheduled to run from November 20 to 22.

Brendan Dolby, vice president of commercial at Las Vegas Grand Prix, Inc., said: “F1 has always been a platform for innovation, and our partnership with Zoox brings that spirit to life in a new way.

“Together, we have an opportunity to showcase the future of mobility on a global stage while building a partnership that extends well beyond race week.”

The new agreement builds on Zoox’s presence in F1, having previously secured a multi-year regional deal with the Williams Racing F1 racing team in 2024.

Under the deal, Zoox has a presence at the Las Vegas Fan Zone and the two other US races in Austin and Miami, with planned activations across Las Vegas throughout race weeks.

Zoox already has a presence in the city, with the company currently providing premium pickup and drop-off services at major hotels, resorts, entertainment venues, and the Harry Reid International Airport.

The company also has a deal in place with NHL ice hockey’s Vegas Golden Knights to serve as the presenting partner for the team’s home game against the Dallas Stars on November 17.

Carly Wyatt, vice president of experience, communications and marketing at Zoox, said: “Partnering with Las Vegas Grand Prix, Inc. brings together a shared commitment to engineering and innovation with the people and energy that make this city so special.

“Our purpose-built robotaxi was designed around the rider to make getting around more seamless, comfortable, and enjoyable. Together, we’re bringing autonomous transportation to one of the world’s most exciting sports and cultural moments.”

For the Las Vegas GP, the new deal adds to the race’s growing commercial portfolio, having secured its place on the F1 calendar until at least 2037 through a 10-year extension announced earlier this year.

Most recently, organizers secured partnerships with IT technology solutions brand Insight Enterprises, as well as SBI Holdings, the Japanese financial services group. The title sponsor for the race is Dutch beer brand Heineken.

title: Ireland's home straight to World Cup starts with Pumas
article_text:
Los Pumas - two words to strike fear into the heart of Ireland rugby fans.

As they return to the Aviva Stadium in the Nations Championship on Friday night, it feels something of an anomaly that a team who have inflicted so much hurt on Ireland over the years have never beaten them in Dublin.

Indeed, out of the 20 previous meetings between these two sides, Ireland have won 14. It is the nature of those handful of losses, however, that have so coloured this rivalry.

Three times the sides have met at the World Cup.

Three times Argentina have won and three times the result has heralded Ireland's early exit from the competition.

With Ireland's first game of Australia 2027 now just under 11 months away, the sight of the blue and white hoops of their frequent tournament nemesis will certainly sharpen the mind.

All the more so given that, should results go in accordance with seeding, the sides would meet at the quarter-final stage on Halloween night in Brisbane.

As he announced his team selection on Wednesday afternoon, Ireland head coach Andy Farrell acknowledged his side are not presently "good enough to board the plane believing that 100%" they are ready to lift the Webb Ellis trophy for the first time.

A year out from the World Cups of 2015, 2019 and 2023, Ireland had enjoyed banner seasons, and by this stage were eagerly anticipating the tournaments to come.

While that has not been the case through 2026 to date, the head coach added that he is excited by the thought of the work still to do.

If wider optimism around next year feels in short supply, it is because Ireland's issues have come to bear when playing the very best.

Across the past two years, their only six defeats have come in the six games they have played against New Zealand, South Africa and France. All came via double-digit scores.

As such, the eye has long been drawn to the visit of the Springboks to Dublin on 21 November, but there can be no looking past a dangerous Argentina fixture.

The Pumas will be expected to provide a good yardstick for both the collective and a number of individuals in an intriguing selection.

With Jack Crowley injured, Sam Prendergast has another opportunity to grab the 10 jersey. When the then 21-year-old made his debut in this fixture two years ago, it certainly felt like a selection with the future, and the 2027 World Cup, in mind.

The Leinster player has had an uneven start to his Test career, and had lost his place in even his provincial 23 by the time of last season's Champions Cup final, but has the chance to lay down a real marker this month.

Farrell has also put his faith in two regular bench options from the start.

For all the talk of Prendergast's readiness to be Johnny Sexton's long-term successor at fly-half, the now assistant coach's role as the backline's cerebral fulcrum has already been assumed by Jamison Gibson-Park.

Arguably Ireland's most important player during this World Cup cycle, the scrum-half missed the start of the season with a groin injury but was player of the match in his return against Munster at the Aviva Stadium.

He will start this window on the bench with Craig Casey instead getting the nod. The 27-year-old will win his 31st cap on Friday but will be making just a second start against a side currently in the top eight of the world rankings.

It is a similar story for Nick Timoney, preferred here to Josh van der Flier, who has become a trusted bench option over the past 12 months but gets a start against this level of opposition for the first time.

Without Caelan Doris and Jack Conan through injury, how the Ulster flanker, Sean Jansen and Ryan Baird fare against what is an abrasive Argentina back row should have a big impact on the game.

While United Rugby Championship results for Irish sides this season have been poor - the provinces have combined for just six wins, three of them by Leinster - key players should at least be more battle-hardened than a year ago.

Then, with so many coming off the British and Irish Lions tour of Australia last summer, most had only one game under their belt when looking so flat during their defeat by New Zealand in Chicago. Now, at least, many frontliners have featured in multiple club games before making the jump back to Test-level rugby.

Argentina, however, certainly seem more primed than they have been for recent windows too.

Head coach Felipe Contepomi has spoken of historic significance of chasing a first away win over Ireland, even if 12 of his matchday squad have recent fond memories of the Aviva Stadium from their win over the Lions there 17 months ago.

The side have lost 12 of 18 Tests since that famous win, although Contepomi, like so many of his predecessors, has had difficulties with player availability as a southern hemisphere team whose squad is mainly based in the north.

While there are absentees for this tour - most notably Bath's Santiago Carreras and Lyon prop Thomas Gallo - the 12 changes made from the 28-28 draw with Australia in September undoubtedly have strengthened a starting side with 750 caps' worth of Test experience.

Coupled with the addition of Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma to Contepomi's coaching staff, Los Pumas feel more than capable of giving Ireland exactly the sort of challenge needed as the World Cup looms ever closer on the horizon.

title: Newmark brings commercial real estate into the Knicks and Rangers sponsorship ecosystem
article_text:
Newmark has entered into a new partnership with two of New York’s most prominent sports franchises, becoming the official commercial real estate partner of the New York Knicks and New York Rangers.

The agreement also extends across the Madison Square Garden portfolio, strengthening the real estate advisory firm’s association with the city’s sports and entertainment industry.

The partnership designates Newmark as an official partner of Madison Square Garden and the official commercial real estate partner of the Westchester Knicks, the NBA G League affiliate of the New York Knicks.

The agreement provides Newmark with a range of branding and promotional opportunities across the franchises and their home venues. These include dasherboard advertising and LED ribbon signage during Knicks and Rangers home games at Madison Square Garden, alongside digitally enhanced dasherboard placements during regular-season home and away games broadcast on MSG Networks.

Newmark will also become the presenting partner of content featured on a Rangers social media platform ahead of every regular-season game. Additional visibility will come through digital signage outside Madison Square Garden and courtside LED advertising during Westchester Knicks home games at the Westchester County Centre.

Doug Jossem, Executive Vice President Global Sports and Entertainment Partnerships, MSG Entertainment, said, “We’re proud to welcome Newmark, one of the world’s foremost commercial real estate firms with deep ties to New York City, to our roster of marketing partners. Bringing together a leading global commercial real estate advisor and service provider and one of the most recognisable sports and entertainment destinations, this partnership delivers meaningful value for both organisations, and we are looking forward to bringing it to life.”

Barry Gosin, Chief Executive Officer of Newmark, added, “Madison Square Garden is one of the most iconic and influential venues in the world, synonymous with excellence, innovation and the energy of New York City. Newmark was founded in Manhattan and is deeply connected to this city’s business community, so we’re proud to partner with an organisation that shares our commitment to excellence, innovation and delivering exceptional experiences.”

The partnership reflects the growing appeal of professional sports properties to business-to-business brands seeking to strengthen corporate relationships and engage with influential audiences. For Newmark, the association provides a platform to reinforce its brand presence across sports, broadcast and digital channels while connecting with the wider New York business ecosystem.

title: OneCourt, NHL activating through Ticketmaster sponsorship
article_text:
Accessibility tech startup OneCourt and the NHL reached a deal to bring the company’s haptic devices for blind and low-vision fans to the league’s tentpole events. The activation, which comes in collaboration with sponsor Ticketmaster, kicked off at last week’s Tim Hortons NHL Heritage Classic and will also bring OneCourt to the Discover NHL Winter Classic, Honda NHL All-Star, and Navy Federal Credit Union NHL Stadium Series.

OneCourt -- the Sports Technology of the Year winner at SBA: Tech in May -- has an in-venue product featuring haptics along with a surface that outlines the field of competition. By combining that device with game tracking data, vibrations turn into low-latency play-by-play for users. For NHL games, OneCourt is ingesting the league’s NHL Edge puck- and player-tracking data.

On top of the league connection, the Avalanche, Blackhawks, Capitals and Red Wings will have OneCourt devices at all of their home games this season. Ticketmaster’s sponsorship has helped OneCourt spread throughout professional sports: nine NBA teams deployed OneCourt with the help of the ticketing giant, along with the previously mentioned NHL clubs.

Recently, OneCourt supported games at the FIFA Men’s World Cup and is activating around select Seattle Seahawks games. The 2026 Super Bowl included a OneCourt deployment as well. OneCourt is also producing an at-home device, with an official launch sometime in December.

title: Fin Smith fit to face Australia as Ben Curry replaces injured twin Tom in England lineup
article_text:
Fin Smith has successfully come through his final fitness Test to be named at fly-half for England’s autumn opener against Australia while Ben Curry is selected at openside flanker for the first time since the summer of 2025.

Steve Borthwick has made four changes to the side that beat Argentina in July with George Furbank also coming in at fullback, Maro Itoje returning to captain the side and Fin Baxter getting the nod at loosehead prop. The Exeter back-row Greg Fisilau is in line for a debut from the bench.

Smith’s selection is a boost for Borthwick, who lost Tom Curry to an injury sustained in training on Wednesday. The Guardian understands there are concerns that Tom Curry will not be fit to feature at any stage of England’s autumn campaign with twin brother Ben stepping up at openside flanker.

The 24-year-old Smith has started England’s last five matches and has cemented his place as England’s first choice fly-half. Furbank, meanwhile, will make his first appearance for two years as a result of a litany of injuries. He was due to start against South Africa in the summer but was struck down by appendicitis days before the match.

Elsewhere, Itoje comes back into the side after being rested over the summer and takes his place in the second-row alongside Alex Coles. As a result, George Martin must do with a place on the bench, which features a 6-2 split. Baxter’s selection means Ellis Genge is among the replacements to bring ballast from the bench as part of the “Pom Squad”. The Harlequins prop has recovered from a long-term foot injury to make his first appearance since last year’s autumn campaign.

Jack van Poortvliet is picked at scrum-half in the injury absence of Alex Mitchell while Seb Atkinson and Henry Slade reprise their centre partnership. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tommy Freeman continue on the wing. Baxter, Jamie George and Joe Heyes make up the front row while Ollie Chessum and Ben Earl complete the back-row along with Ben Curry.

On the bench, Luke Cowan-Dickie and Will Stuart join Genge in providing front-row back-up while Henry Pollock covers back-row and wing. Ben Spencer and Marcus Smith are the two backs selected among the replacements.

title: Faf de Klerk stood down with immediate effect
article_text:
Faf de Klerk has been ruled out for eight weeks after The Cheetahs confirmed the experienced scrum-half suffered an ankle injury.

The South African was injured during the club's match against Bayonne on October 18 and is expected to return in early January.

The Cheetahs confirmed that De Klerk is targeting a return for their third-round EPCR Challenge Cup clash against Zebre Parma in Italy.

Despite not competing in a European league, the South African side feature in the competition.

De Klerk, who was left out of the Springboks' Nations Championship squad, will be a significant loss for the Cheetahs.

The 35-year-old has won two Rugby World Cups with South Africa, establishing himself as a key figure in their 2019 triumph.

He made his international debut in 2016 before joining Sale Sharks a year later.

De Klerk played a starring role in South Africa's 2019 World Cup campaign, scoring against Japan before starting the final victory over England.

He subsequently moved to Japan's Yokohama Canon Eagles in 2022 before returning to South Africa this year.

His last appearance for the Springboks came against the Barbarians in June, but he has since been overlooked by Rassie Erasmus.

However, the scrum-half has made it clear that his international career is far from over.

De Klerk recently signed a two-year contract with the Cheetahs and has dismissed suggestions that his return to South Africa signals the beginning of retirement.

Despite turning 35 and facing increased competition for the number nine shirt, the experienced scrum-half remains determined to feature at the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

South Africa have considerable depth at scrum-half, with Erasmus giving several players opportunities as he builds towards the tournament.

When De Klerk was omitted earlier this year, the Springboks head coach explained that the decision did not necessarily mark the end of his international career.

Instead, South Africa wanted to assess their other options before finalising their World Cup plans.

That could leave the door open for De Klerk, who played a crucial role in the Springboks' back-to-back World Cup victories in 2019 and 2023.

His immediate focus, however, will be recovering from injury and returning to action with the Cheetahs in January.

title: Former England star set to make Fiji debut after switching international allegiance
article_text:
Former England international Nathan Hughes is set to make his Fiji debut this weekend, seven years after his last appearance for England.

The 35-year-old has been named at number eight for Fiji's Nations Championship clash with France in Lyon on Saturday.

Hughes won 22 caps for England between 2016 and 2019 under Eddie Jones, but will now represent the country of his birth.

The Racing 92 forward will start alongside Pita-Gus Sowakula and Kitione Salawa in Fiji's back row.

Hughes made his England debut against South Africa in November 2016 after impressing for Wasps in the Premiership.

He later played for Bristol Bears and Bath before continuing his career overseas.

Born in Lautoka, Fiji, Hughes qualifies under World Rugby's eligibility regulations, which allow players to switch nations after a three-year stand-down period, subject to birthright requirements and approval.

His return comes under new Fiji head coach Jake White, who has selected the experienced forward for his second match in charge.

Fiji face France on Saturday before taking on Ireland in Dublin on 14 November and Italy the following weekend.

Hughes is one of several players with England experience preparing to represent another nation this autumn.

- 🇹🇴 Manu Vunipola (Tonga): The former England U20 fly-half has been named on Tonga's bench against Romania on Friday. The cousin of Billy and Mako Vunipola could make his senior international debut after completing his switch from England.

- 🇮🇪 Kieran Brookes (Ireland XV): The 36-year-old prop won 16 England caps and featured at the 2015 Rugby World Cup. He has been selected for Ireland XV against Fiji A on 20 November.

- 🇮🇪 Dan Kelly (Ireland XV): The Munster centre won his only England cap against Canada in 2021. He has also been selected for the Fiji A fixture and could push for a place in Ireland's senior squad.

Both Brookes and Kelly have been selected for Ireland's representative XV rather than the senior Test team.

The developments come amid growing uncertainty over the futures of several England-qualified players, with Max Ojomoh also linked with a move away following his latest international snub.

title: Road to the WTA Finals: After the long road to No. 1, Elena Rybakina is ready for another title
article_text:
Road to the WTA Finals: After the long road to No. 1, Elena Rybakina is ready for another title

Editor’s note: Ahead of the year-end tournament, we’re publishing Road to the WTA Finals, an eight-part snapshot of the qualifiers and the form they bring to Indian Wells. Check back all week for new installments.

Fittingly, the final stop on the Road to the 2026 WTA Finals belongs to the player who won the last one. Elena Rybakina arrives in Indian Wells as both the defending champion and the World No. 1, having left Riyadh a year ago unbeaten, with a three-set win over Jessica Pegula in the semifinals and a tight two-setter against Aryna Sabalenka in the final.

She has since turned that week into a season. Rybakina beat Sabalenka again in the Australian Open final, added a clay-court title in Stuttgart and then worked through a demanding fortnight at the US Open, where she needed three sets to get past both Zheng Qinwen and Coco Gauff before outlasting Sabalenka, 6-4, 5-7, 6-2, for her second major of the year.

The top ranking was the reward. When Rybakina officially reached No. 1 on Sept. 14, at 27 years and 89 days, she became the second-oldest player to do so for the first time, behind only Angelique Kerber, and she arrives in California at 54-14 with four titles. Now she can attempt something no one has managed since Serena Williams won three in a row from 2012 to 2014 -- winning the WTA Finals in back-to-back years.

In a nutshell: Rybakina picked up right where she left off in Riyadh. After winning the WTA Finals last year, she opened 2026 with the Australian Open title, added a Stuttgart trophy on clay and bookended her Grand Slam season with another major at the US Open. That victory sent her to No. 1 for the first time, turning an already impressive year into the best of her career. Rybakina will enter the WTA Finals coming off a title in Ningbo just a few weeks ago.

The match that defined her year: There were plenty of candidates, but the US Open final offered the clearest snapshot of how far Rybakina had come. She reached it with three-set wins over Zheng Qinwen and Coco Gauff, then went the distance again against Sabalenka, winning 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 for her second major of the year. Rybakina had also beaten Sabalenka in three sets in the Australian Open final; in New York, she did it after surviving two more tough tests to get there.

One number to know: 27 years, 89 days. That was Rybakina’s age when she officially became world No. 1 on Sept. 14, making her the second-oldest player to reach the top for the first time. Only Kerber, at 28 years, 238 days, was older. It took Rybakina a while to get there, but she’s looked right at home since.

In her words: "I always believed it was possible. … Of course, along your journey, you learn a lot, many things happen. I feel I now have a great team, great people around me, and we just keep working. Finally, everything has paid off.” -- Rybakina after winning the US Open and ascending to the World No. 1.

Hottest hot shot: This was your typical half volley pickup, a lob run down all the way to the baseline, and then a lob of her own sent back over Maria Sakkari, who was left at the net with nothing to do but turn around and watch it land. That was Rybakina in the opening round in Rome back in May, pulling a winner out of a point that she had no business winning -- until she did.

What she’s chasing: Rybakina put together a dominant, undefeated campaign at the 2025 WTA Finals in Riyadh, where she opened up with a seamless win against Amanda Anisimova before ultimately taking down Pegula in three sets in the semifinals and Sabalenka in a tight two-setter to win the title.

Now, Rybakina is looking to become the first player since Serena Williams (who won three straight from 2012 to 2014) to win back-to-back WTA Finals.

title: Tennis-WTA Finals to test endurance, nerve in Indian Wells
article_text:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - The WTA Finals will offer the season's elite a final test of consistency, resilience and composure, with defending champion Elena Rybakina and rival Aryna Sabalenka set to lead the field in the California desert, former player and Tennis Channel analyst Chanda Rubin said.

The season-ending championship brings together the year's top eight players, a distinction Rubin said reflects not just peak performance but the ability to withstand the demands of a long calendar.

"It's a big title," Rubin told Reuters. "If you can be one of the best eight players at the end of the season, it means you have had not only a great year, but a consistent year in some shape or fashion."

The round-robin format adds another layer of difficulty, with players facing elite opposition from their opening match rather than building gradually through an early draw.

"The players who can come through the group-stage play, those are the ones that truly understand how to build," Rubin said. "That's indicative of what they've done all year."

Rybakina arrives with the year-end world number one ranking secured and a chance to defend the title she won a year ago when the tournament was held in Riyadh. Rubin said the understated Kazakh has repeatedly shown her ability to deliver under pressure.

"She loves to win, and she is so low-key that she's one of the best competitors out there," Rubin said. "She has been able to respond time and time again throughout the year on big occasions, on big stages."

A second straight Finals crown would underline Rybakina's position at the summit of the women's game, Rubin added.

"Any time you can come back and defend a title, win it back-to-back years, that says a lot," she said. "It's something special. It's not something that players can do all the time."

Sabalenka, meanwhile, will arrive with a different kind of incentive after losing last year's final to Rybakina and falling to her at this year's Australian Open and US Open.

Rubin said the Belarusian's powerful game makes her a threat to any opponent, but that managing her emotions could prove decisive.

"For so long now she has been the hunted," Rubin said. "It's different when now she's got something to chase."

With Rybakina holding the top ranking, Sabalenka may benefit from the shift in pressure, Rubin said.

"Maybe that releases a little bit of the tension. Maybe that relaxes her a little bit more," she said. "With a big game, you've got to have the balance — the mental and emotional part of it — because otherwise it can go sideways."

Rybakina opens Group One play on Sunday against Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova as part of a quartet that includes Americans Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula.

Sabalenka, the world number two, heads Group Two with 19-year-old Mirra Andreeva, former champion Elina Svitolina and Czech Karolina Muchova.

title: Korea Open: American Pursuit Gathers Momentum
article_text:
World No.15 Lauren Lam/Allison Quynh Lee continued their march towards a historic breakthrough on Friday, reaching the semifinal of the YEOSU VICTOR Korea Open 2026 with a 21-19 21-10 win over Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva.

The result marks the Americans’ third Super 500 semifinal of the season, adding to a campaign that has also featured a Super 300 semifinal and established them as genuine contenders on the HSBC BWF World Tour.

For a pair seeking to become the first American women’s doubles partnership to win a World Tour title, Yeosu represents another significant step forward. It also comes at an important time for American badminton, with the countdown already under way to the opening of the qualification period for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games next year. With badminton preparing for a rare moment in the spotlight on home soil, Lam/Lee’s continued rise is providing further evidence that the United States can field genuine contenders when qualification begins.

The quarterfinal presented a unique challenge. Across the net stood not only accomplished opponents but close friends and long-time idols.

“It was a fight of the nerves,” Lee told BWF.

Having spent countless hours together on and off court, both pairs entered the quarterfinals with a deep understanding of each other’s strengths and tendencies.

The opening game reflected that familiarity, with neither side able to establish control. Lam/Lee eventually edged ahead at the crucial moments before taking command in the second game to complete a convincing victory.

Lam admitted the emotional aspect of the contest was more difficult before the first shuttle was struck than during the match itself.

“When it was love-all, I was just kind of focused and locked in,” she said. “That feeling just naturally went away.”

The Americans’ rise has not happened overnight. Competing as independent players, they shared the significant sacrifices in pursuit of their ambitions on tour.

“We put everything into this,” Lee said. “We put school on hold. We put on hold on a lot of things, like friendships back at home. We still keep in contact, but obviously we can’t see them all the time, so a lot of sacrifices are put into this, so it does feel really good.”

Their success has also coincided with growing momentum for American badminton across several disciplines.

“I’m really happy that we’re all kind of raising the bar,” Lam said.

Despite another career milestone, neither player is looking beyond the next match.

“We just want to perform well, and then everything else will follow,” Lee said.

That approach has already carried Lam/Lee to another semifinal. Now, with their consistency at Super 500 level becoming impossible to ignore, the prospect of a first World Tour title no longer feels like a distant ambition but an increasingly realistic goal.

They will play Rui Hirokami/Sayaka Hobara for the first time in the semifinals.

title: "Second BWF Title of the Season": Kiren Rijiju Congratulates PV Sindhu on HYLO Open 2026 Triumph
article_text:
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Friday congratulated Indian badminton star PV Sindhu on winning the HYLO Open 2026 in Germany, marking her second title on the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour this season.

Rijiju met the two-time Olympic medallist and her husband, Venkata Datta Sai, and shared a celebratory moment following her victory. He also extended his best wishes to the shuttler for her upcoming tournaments.

"Congratulated @Pvsindhu1 on winning HYLO Open 2026 in Germany! Glad to meet her & Venkata Datta Sai and share the special moment. My best wishes to her for the upcoming tournaments!" Rijiju wrote in a post on X.

Sindhu clinched the women's singles title with a commanding 21-12, 21-14 victory over Denmark's Line Kjaersfeldt in the final.

The Indian shuttler produced a dominant performance in Germany, bouncing back from her runner-up finish at the French Open a week earlier. She had lost the final there to South Korean world number one An Se Young.

In the opening game against Kjaersfeldt, Sindhu made a confident start, although the Danish player initially kept the contest competitive. Kjaersfeldt tested the Indian across the court and brought the score to 5-5 before Sindhu began to take control.

Sindhu entered the interval with an 11-8 advantage and used sharp returns and attacking strokes to widen the gap, eventually closing out the game 21-12.

The second game saw Kjaersfeldt put up a stronger challenge, reducing Sindhu's early 7-3 lead to 7-6. However, the Indian regained control by forcing errors and moving her opponent around the court.

Sindhu led 11-7 at the interval and extended her advantage to 19-11. Despite a late attempt by Kjaersfeldt to narrow the deficit, the Indian held her nerve to seal the match 21-14.

The HYLO Open victory marks Sindhu's second BWF World Tour title of 2026. She had earlier won the Japan Open in July.

The latest triumph comes after an impressive run at the French Open, where she reached the final before losing to An Se Young.

The HYLO Open title adds to Sindhu's growing list of achievements as she continues her campaign on the international badminton circuit.

title: What are the Nitto ATP Finals qualification scenarios?
article_text:
Only two singles places remain in the Nitto ATP Finals, with four players in contention for those spots.

Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar are currently are currently in qualifying position. But Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul have a chance to shake things up at the Rolex Paris Masters, where they are still competing.

In quarter-final action Friday, Fritz will face Carlos Alcaraz and Paul will play Ben Shelton.

Tiafoe, who is trying to make his Nitto ATP Finals debut, will qualify as long as Paul does not defeat Fritz in the Paris final.

Jodar, who is also trying to qualify for the first time, will earn his place in Turin if Alcaraz defeats Fritz in their quarter-final and Paul does not reach the final.

Fritz also has a chance to lock in his fourth appearance at the prestigious season-ending event. The 29-year-old American will qualify if he reaches the final, or he reaches semi-finals and Paul does not reach the final.

Paul can make his Turin debut if he wins the title in Paris, or reaches the final and Fritz does not reach the final.

The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals will take place in Turin, Italy, from 15-22 November. Alexander Zverev, Alcaraz, Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Arthur Fils have already qualified.

title: Sergio Garcia makes Ryder Cup admission after positive Luke Donald talks
article_text:
Sergio Garcia has revealed he has already held positive talks with Luke Donald and Justin Rose as he targets a sensational return to the European Ryder Cup team at Adare Manor in 2027.

The Spaniard, who has confirmed his departure from LIV Golf after five years with the breakaway league, is preparing to return to a full schedule on the DP World Tour next season, with a place in Donald's team firmly on his radar.

Garcia, 46, made his Ryder Cup ambitions clear during an exclusive interview with GolfMagic this week, admitting that he would love to represent Europe once again in Ireland next September.

The former Masters champion remains the all-time record points scorer in Ryder Cup history, having accumulated an impressive 28.5 points across 10 appearances. That puts him 3.5 points clear of Sir Nick Faldo, who sits second on the all-time list.

Garcia made his Ryder Cup debut at Brookline in 1999, the same year he turned professional, before making his most recent appearance at Whistling Straits in 2021.

Should he make Donald's team at Adare Manor, Garcia would also match Faldo and Lee Westwood for a joint-record 11 appearances in the European Ryder Cup team.

"I think everyone knows how much I love the Ryder Cup, and I just hope that I can be involved," Garcia told GolfMagic, with nearly 10 months to go until Europe's biennial contest with Jim Furyk's Team USA.

"Obviously I would love to be a part of it as a player. Justin [Rose] and some of the guys have shown that you can do it, even at our age.

"So yeah, if I didn’t think I had the chance then I wouldn’t be saying or trying to make it into the team. What I have to do is go out there and work hard, give it everything that I have, and see what the end result is at the end of the day, and then we will see if there is the possibility of being there as a player, which would be amazing."

Garcia was particularly surprised to learn during the interview that a return to the European team would see him equal Faldo and Westwood's record.

"I knew it was my 11th appearance if I make it, but I didn’t know it was a joint record so thanks for letting me know!" added Garcia.

Garcia's return to the DP World Tour in 2027 will be a significant step in his bid to get back into the European Ryder Cup fold.

The Spaniard has already spoken to captain Donald about his ambitions, with the Englishman supportive of Garcia's efforts to earn a place in the team.

"I had a little chat with Luke in Ireland, mentioning that I was trying as hard as I could to make the team, and he said that he didn’t expect anything else, so that was nice," revealed Garcia.

"I also told him that obviously if I couldn’t be there as a player that I would love to help in any way possible."

Garcia has also held conversations with several members of Donald's European team, including seven-time Ryder Cup player Justin Rose.

While the Spaniard has not spoken extensively with Rory McIlroy about his potential return, he believes there is support among the European players for him to be involved in some capacity.

"I haven’t really talked to Rory [McIlroy] about it much, but I have talked to Justin Rose and a couple of others, and obviously they are on the same page," added Garcia.

"If there is any way that I can help then they are happy for me to be there and that’s what I’m going to try to do. So we’ll see what the year brings us."

Garcia currently remains ineligible to become a future European Ryder Cup captain or vice-captain under the existing Ryder Cup Europe rules, following his previous termination of DP World Tour membership during his time with LIV Golf.

However, he has made it clear that his desire to help Europe goes beyond simply making the playing team.

"As long as I can help the team, I’m happy to be there," Garcia continued.

"If I can do it as a player or any other way I can do it, it would be great. I just want to help as much as possible."

Garcia is also preparing for a significant off-season as he looks to rediscover his best golf ahead of his return to the DP World Tour.

The Spaniard admitted that his short game, wedge play and putting will be among his biggest areas of focus, with his recent switch to a broomstick putter having helped improve his confidence on the greens.

"There are many parts of the game that you can always improve, but I feel like my putting since I went to the broomstick has gotten better and it feels better, which is great, so I am going to keep working on that," said Garcia.

"I am also going to keep working on my short game, chipping, wedge game, it’s an area where I can improve quite a bit.

"Obviously my driving and my long game is usually in good shape, but you can always keep working hard on it and keep improving it.

"So yeah, will be working hard on all those areas, but especially my wedge game, chipping and my putting the most."

Garcia also intends to continue working on the mental side of his game following his outburst at the Masters in April, when he smashed his driver in anger on the second tee during the final round at Augusta National.

title: Rory McIlroy: Why LIV Golf demise is 'amazing' news
article_text:
After making a slice of personal history in Abu Dhabi, Rory McIlroy reflected on the news of LIV Golf’s demise.

Not in 21 years and 1,014 rounds on the DP World Tour had Rory McIlroy ever made 11 birdies in a competitive round. But just 24 hours after accepting a two-shot penalty which seemed a significant blow to his hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai, McIlroy conjured another magical personal record as he surged into contention at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

McIlroy’s 9-under par 63 lit up the second round at Yas Links, a blitz that included seven birdies on the back nine. It all came after taking an unplayable and making bogey on the first, as well as the rules incident that threatened to spoil a solid start to his tournament.

McIlroy was pinged two strokes on Thursday for improving his lie on the 12th hole, volunteering the penalty as he would “much rather be two shots worse off than be called a cheat”.

His playing partner and Race to Dubai rivals were on his side. Eugenio Chacarra was prepared to fight McIlroy’s corner after the incident, while the Northern Irishman laughed that “even Patrick [Reed] was too, surprisingly enough, which is very nice”.

“But at the same time,” he added, “I’d rather take the penalty and not have any room for interpretation.

” I wouldn’t want anyone else in the field thinking I’d got away with it. But at the same time, there’s probably only a handful of us that get our every shot recorded, so that does make it a bit of a grey area. But that comes with the territory.”

In any other week, a rules infringement involving McIlroy would dominate discussion, but the demise of LIV Golf has taken top billing. McIlroy was asked by TG about the news that emerged overnight in US bankruptcy court that LIV is no more.

“It was always going to be very hard for them to get enough players to sign up for what they were proposing which was smaller prize money, no upfront payments,” he said.

“Equity in the league is one thing. They’ve always faced a lot of headwinds from the inception in 2022 but there was no way. If they couldn’t make $6 billion work, they were never going to make $300 million work. The math didn’t add up.”

Earlier this week, Adam Scott told TG that LIV players hoping to join the PGA Tour should be made to “re-qualify”.

Jon Rahm has admitted he “seriously doubts” he will now be offered a deal as generous as the one Brooks Koepka accepted to return to the US circuit from LIV, and McIlroy believes the DP World Tour is going to be the real winner from LIV’s demise.

Alongside Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton, McIlroy’s home circuit could also become a landing ground for the likes of Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Joaquin Niemann. DeChambeau would be able to take up a membership category as a recent major winner, while Johnson and Niemann could both accept tournament invites under a new policy to accommodate the stars left in limbo.

“It would be an amazing thing for this tour if all those guys were funnelled through the DP World Tour and were made to qualify that way,” he said. “I think that’s the right scenario and the right decision and also makes this tour incredibly strong.

“It’s only going to be into the Championship Series. It’s only going to be a handful of cards so it’s going to be very, very competitive.”

title: World No. 1 Seo-Kim Pair Stage Comeback Victory After Seven Months
article_text:
Seo Seung-jae and Kim Won-ho defeated the Chinese pair Wang Chang-Xi Haonan 2-1 (21-14, 15-21, 21-19) in the men's doubles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) held on November 6 at the Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium.

[OSEN=Yeosu, Ko Seong-hwan Reporter] The 'world No. 1' Seo Seung-jae-Kim Won-ho pair (Samsung Life Insurance) achieved a dramatic comeback victory through their relentless determination. The two players, who barely advanced to the semifinals, vowed in front of Korean fans to secure their first victory in about seven months.

Seo Seung-jae and Kim Won-ho defeated the Chinese pair Wang Chang-Xi Haonan 2-1 (21-14, 15-21, 21-19) in the men's doubles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) held on November 6 at the Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium.

It was a tough battle. The Seo-Kim pair won the first game 21-14 with stable defense and exquisite attacks. However, they lost the second game 15-21, overwhelmed by the Chinese pair's strong counterattack.

The third game also brought a crisis. The Seo-Kim pair started strong at 3-0 but allowed the opponents to score five consecutive points, losing momentum. With unforced errors piling up, the score gap widened to 11-16.

However, the world No. 1's prowess was formidable. The Seo-Kim pair scored five straight points to tie at 16-16 and surged ahead to reach match point first at 20-18.

The longest rally of the day, which decided the match, was the highlight. Seo Seung-jae barely received the shuttlecock even after falling on the court. He got back up to continue his defense and finally scored the decisive point, putting an end to the intense battle.

In the mixed zone after the match, Seo Seung-jae reflected, "I think that movement came from trying to receive the shuttle no matter what. Even though I fell, I quickly got up thinking that if I could somehow return one more shot, Kim Won-ho would cover for me."

It was a nerve-wracking moment for Kim Won-ho, who was watching from behind. He smiled and said, "There were many tense moments throughout. Especially in the final moments, my racket broke. I was relieved that Seung-jae defended and finished the point."

The driving force behind their three-game comeback victory was their trust in each other. Seo Seung-jae stated, "Even though we were trailing, I thought good chances would come if we kept playing well until the end. Today, we challenged ourselves with the mindset of not giving up until the end and following each point."

Partner Kim Won-ho also emphasized, "We could have collapsed during the third game. However, we maintained trust in Seung-jae until the end and kept fighting without giving up. The fans' enthusiastic support also gave us more strength."

Another driving force repeatedly emphasized by the two players was the passionate support from home fans. The spectators at Jinnam Gymnasium that day did not hesitate to encourage the pair even in moments when the match seemed to be slipping away.

Kim Won-ho said, "Since this is a tournament held in Korea, I think the good results were possible thanks to the support from many spectators. I consider it an honor," crediting the fans. Seo Seung-jae also conveyed, "Although there were many difficulties, we were able to come back and win thanks to the support from many fans. I would like to express my gratitude."

Now, the Seo-Kim pair are challenging for their second consecutive Korea Open title and a victory after about seven months. Since reuniting in early 2025, they have won an impressive 11 tournaments. However, this year, after winning the Malaysia Open in January, the All England Open in March, and the Asian Championships in April, they failed to reach the top in nine consecutive tournaments.

Seo Seung-jae emphasized, "If we win in Korea, I think we can use it as a springboard to play even better. I really want to win this time." Kim Won-ho also pledged, "Last year, we won many unexpected titles, so we end up making comparisons. I think we are doing well enough even now. Above all, I am grateful to be injury-free. Since this is the last tournament held in Korea, I will do my best to win."

title: SeatGeek extends ticketing deals with Eredivisie trio
article_text:
SeatGeek, the digital ticketing platform, has consolidated its presence in Dutch soccer’s top-tier Eredivisie by extending its commercial partnerships with clubs AZ Alkmaar, PEC Zwolle, and PSV Eindhoven.

Under the renewed agreement, SeatGeek will continue to serve as the official ticketing partner of the three clubs, providing supporters with one place to buy, manage, and use their tickets.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The company will also continue to help the clubs use data, technology, and fan insights to run efficiently and build deeper fan connections.

Coen Schroots, ticketing & fan services manager at PSV Eindhoven, said: “We’re pleased to continue our longstanding relationship with SeatGeek as we roll out enhanced ticketing functionality to improve the experience for our supporters and give our team greater flexibility in managing sales and ticketing operations.

“SeatGeek’s understanding of PSV and our ambitions provides a strong foundation for our continued collaboration.”

The three deals build on SeatGeek’s decade-long presence within the league through its partnership with the Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB), which saw the company support ticketing across the Eredivisie.

During that time, SeatGeek has worked with each Eredivisie club on its ticketing needs and matchday goals.

Jordan Hitchen, regional director, EMEA at SeatGeek, said: “The Netherlands has become one of SeatGeek’s most important markets in Europe, and each renewal reflects the strength of the relationships we’ve built with our clubs over many years.

“We’ve learned a lot by working alongside all three clubs, and we’re looking forward to building on that work – giving each the flexibility to keep improving its ticketing experience for supporters as their needs evolve.”

The renewals come as SeatGeek continues to solidify its place among top European soccer properties, having secured long-term extensions with English soccer’s Manchester City, Leeds United and Newcastle United this year.

title: Nestle Confectionery added to Everton Women commercial slate
article_text:
Everton Women, of English soccer’s top-tier Women’s Super League, have secured Nestle Confectionary, the chocolates and sweet division of the multinational food and drinks giant, as a new commercial partner.

The new agreement will see Nestle Confectionary serve as the official chocolate and grab sweet partner of Everton Women and an official supplier of Hill Dickinson Stadium – the club’s official main stadium – and the women's team's home ground of Goodison Park.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As part of the partnership, popular Nestle brands including KitKat, Smarties, Rowntree’s Aero, Lion, Yorkie, Milkybar, and Quality Street will feature across both venues.

Nestle will also gain a prominent presence at Goodison Park via pitchside LED advertising, big-screen exposure, and matchday activations designed to engage supporters and showcase the company’s products at food kiosks and points of sale.

Hill Dickinson Stadium will also stock Nestle’s products.

Gail Stove, out-of home confectionery lead for Nestlé UK & Ireland, said: “Nestlé Confectionery is excited to be an official partner of Everton Women and official supplier of Hill Dickinson Stadium.

“Working collaboratively with Everton Football Club, we’ll bring the No.1 confectionery single within the leisure channel, KitKat 4 Finger, along with other iconic Nestlé Confectionery brands for everyone to enjoy.”

Everton Women play some matches at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, home ground of the Everton men’s team, due to WSL rules that require clubs to host at least one home match per season at their nominated main stadium.

While Goodison Park serves as Everton Women’s everyday home ground, Hill Dickinson Stadium remains officially designated as the club’s main stadium.

Andrew Middleton, president of business operations at Everton, said: “Like Everton, Nestlé’s brands have been part of family life for generations, making this a natural fit for our supporters and matchday experience.

“This partnership is another important step in Everton Women’s continued growth, and we look forward to working with Nestlé to bring it to life.”

The partnership marks the second dedicated commercial partnership for Everton Women after last year’s deal secured with catering company GGM Gastro. Other sponsorship agreements are tied in with the men’s team.

The new partnership comes a month after it was reported that the Friedkin Group, the business and investment consortium led by US businessman Dan Friedkin, is seeking to sell off at least a part of its stake in Everton.

Friedkin acquired a majority stake in Everton in December 2024 from Farhad Moshiri and his Blue Heaven Holdings, with the club experiencing significant financial difficulty and on-pitch struggles.

Now, less than two years later, the group is exploring a partial or full sale of its holdings in the club, tapping investment bank Moelis & Company to lead the sales process.

Everton was Friedkin’s third European soccer acquisition after Italian heavyweights AS Roma in 2020, and French third-tier side AS Cannes (who were in the fourth tier at the time).

In May 2026, Forbes valued Everton at $930 million, 25th among all soccer clubs globally, owing largely to its 52,769-seater Hill Dickinson Stadium (the newest venue in the Premier League) and annual revenues of $255 million.

title: Gloucestershire to rebrand as Bristol for T20 Blast from 2027
article_text:
Gloucestershire Cricket will rebrand its men’s and women’s T20 Blast teams under a Bristol identity from 2027, following a 21% drop in competition revenue this year.

The club, which has competed as Gloucestershire in every format since 1870, set out the plan to members at the Seat Unique Stadium in Bristol, according to the BBC. A second members’ meeting is scheduled in Cheltenham. The club says players, members, stakeholders and the ECB were consulted over several months.

Gloucestershire will remain the club’s overarching identity, and the county name will be kept for other formats. The new T20 name, kit and logo are expected to be revealed alongside the 2027 Blast fixtures on 24th November.

The Blast accounts for 20% of the club’s ticketing revenue. While overall attendances are rising, income from the competition has fallen since Gloucestershire won the title in 2024, beating Somerset at Edgbaston for the county’s first trophy in nine years.

The move echoes Warwickshire’s 2014 rebrand as the Birmingham Bears, which the club credited with record attendances and higher commercial income. Warwickshire reversed the decision this season after feedback from members, and returned as the Warwickshire Bears.

Neil Priscott, Chief Executive Officer of Gloucestershire Cricket, told members the club planned to “invest in Gloucestershire’s future – strengthening our club identity as we pursue our top-eight ambition, while creating a distinct Bristol-based T20 team to reach a new audience.”

In a statement, the club said, “As part of our wider strategic vision to grow domestic cricket, attract new audiences across the region, and drive commercial reinvestment back into the sport, we will be creating a new dedicated T20 identity for our men’s and women’s teams.”

Stuart Cain, Chief Executive Officer of Warwickshire, said of his club’s reversal, “The club decided to be bold with a city-based name for our T20 team, and it saw attendances grow to record levels and attract new fans to the Bears. But with our long-term future in mind, and following feedback from members, now is the right time for change.”

title: Magnus Norman speaks for the first time after becoming Jannik Sinner’s new coach
article_text:
After weeks of speculation, Magnus Norman has finally been confirmed as Jannik Sinner’s new coach.

In an Instagram video, Sinner announced that he would be parting ways Darren Cahill after four years, and five Grand Slam title wins, together.

Norman, meanwhile, has just ended his long-standing partnership with Stan Wawrinka, who has just played his final-ever competitive match in tennis.

Sinner announced the news that he would be working with Magnus Norman and now the Swedish coach has shared a statement on the upcoming collaboration.

In a post via Norman’s academy Good to Great, the Swede said: “First of all, I have enormous respect for the work Darren Cahill and the entire team have done with Jannik Sinner over the years.

“They have done an incredible job, and I feel privileged to have the opportunity to build on what they have achieved. Jannik is obviously already one of the best players in the world, but what excited me most is his personality and mindset.

“He is still young, very humble and incredibly hungry to learn and improve, despite everything he has already accomplished. For me, that is what makes working with him so exciting.

“I’m really looking forward to being part of his team and contributing in any way I can to his continued development.”

Sinner and Norman are set to work together in the off-season at the Italian’s home in Monte Carlo ahead of the 2027 season.

That implies that Sinner is closing in on a return to tennis after missing the second half of the season due to a knee injury.

It’s likely that his next competitive tournament will be the Australian Open, which takes place at the end of January, as Sinner does not tend to play a warm-up event Down Under.

Both Sinner and Norman have experience of winning the tournament, with the Italian claiming two titles in 2024 and 2025 and the Swede guiding Wawrinka to the 2014 title in Melbourne.

Between them, Sinner and Norman have currently won eight Grand Slams between them, so they should be a force to be reckoned with in the 2027 season.

2027 looks to be dominated by top, new coaching collaborations, with Juan Carlos Ferrero working with Ben Shelton and Felix Auger-Aliassime getting to grips with Ivan Ljubicic as his new coach.

Norman will be hoping to fit in seamlessly with Sinner’s other coach, Simone Vagnozzi, who worked tirelessly alongside Cahill in their very successful four years together.

Sinner will be the fourth player Norman has worked with on the ATP Tour, following partnerships with Thomas Johansson, Robin Soderling, and Wawrinka.

title: The Paris Masters crowd branded ‘clowns’ by ATP star after raucous behaviour
article_text:
French crowds are normally some of the more riotous crowds in tennis and the Paris Masters has been no different.

The home crowd at the Plenitude Arena have been loud and proud for Frenchman and they have been rewarded with several deep runs at the tournament.

Luca Van Assche has produced a dream run to the quarterfinals, while the likes of Quentin Halys, Arthur Rinderknech, and Arthur Fils all reaching the third round.

However, the Paris Masters crowd has been called into question for their behaviour during a non-French player match, between Rinky Hijikata and Tomas Martin Etcheverry.

The pair played out an enthralling third round contest, as Hijikata reached his first Masters quarterfinal by beating the Argentine in three sets.

However, after the match, Hijikata suggested he was far from happy with the conduct of some members of the crowd during his match againts Etcheverry.

“He had some pretty raucous fans out there that were being clowns,” said the Australian during his post-match interviews at the Paris Masters, in his inimitable Aussie style.

However, Hijikata saw the positive side of the ‘clownish behaviour. He said he used that to battle his way into the quarterfinals of the competition, where he will face Frenchman Luca van Assche for a place in the semifinals.

“They kind of fired me up,” admitted the star, who currently sits at world No 59 in the ATP Tour live rankings. “Without them I probably wouldn’t have been able to get going. So thanks to those guys.”

Hijikata has enjoyed a Paris Masters to remember after defeating Jaime Faria and Vit Kopriva to gain access to the ATP 1000 main draw.

He has beaten Luciano Darderi, Novak Djokovic, and Tomas Martin Etcheverry in the main draw, all of whom are ranked significantly higher than him.

If he continues his progress through the tournament, there is an outside chance he can gain seeded entry into his home Grand Slam at the Australian Open next year.

The top 32 ranked players are awarded seeded status and Hijikata is currently 27 places away from that. With 800 ranking points still to play for in Paris, Hijikata could soar up the rankings before the tournament reaches its conclusion.

Hijikata has been joined in the quarterfinals of the Paris Masters by van Assche, Carlos Alcaraz, Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud, Ben Shelton, Tommy Paul, and Nuno Borges.

The Paris Masters is set to conclude with the final on November 8th and Hijikata will absolutely be hoping he can be one of the two players battling for the title.

title: Hyrox Kuala Lumpur gets green light after alcohol sponsorship row
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: This year's controversial Hyrox Kuala Lumpur has been granted conditional approval after its organisers agreed to comply fully with the Safe Sport Code, ending uncertainty over whether the fitness event would go ahead.

Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari said the approval was issued under Section 33 of the Sports Development Act 1997 (Act 576), subject to the organisers meeting all requirements under the code and conditions imposed by the Sports Commissioner's Office.

"The organisers of Hyrox Kuala Lumpur have agreed to fully comply with Article 5.2 of the Safe Sport Code," said Taufiq in a statement.

He said the ministry would monitor compliance throughout the event, which is scheduled to take place from Dec 10-13 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC).

The development follows the ministry's Nov 4 statement outlining its position on the event after controversy erupted over an alcohol sponsorship arrangement.

Article 5.2 of the Safe Sport Code prohibits companies involved in tobacco, electronic cigarettes and alcoholic beverages from organising, sponsoring, promoting, advertising or displaying their trademarks at sporting events approved or supported by the ministry and its agencies.

The ministry had warned that approval would not be granted unless the sponsorship issue was resolved, including the removal of related branding and promotional materials.

With the conditions now accepted, Taufiq said mass fitness events such as Hyrox should continue to be encouraged for promoting an active and healthy lifestyle among Malaysians.

"Mass fitness events such as this should continue to be encouraged as they promote an active and healthy lifestyle among Malaysians," he said.

Taufiq also wished all participants the best of luck in the competition.

[OSEN=Yeosu, Ko Seong-hwan Reporter] South Korean badminton produced a women’s doubles pair advancing to the semifinals on home soil. The Kim You-jung-Lee Yu-rim pair (Samsung Life Insurance) secured a spot in the semifinals with a come-from-behind victory over a Chinese team.

Kim You-jung-Lee Yu-rim (World No. 31) defeated the Chinese pair Li Yijing-Wang Yiduo (World No. 93) with a game score of 2-1 (17-21, 21-8, 22-20) in the women’s doubles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) held at the Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City on the 6th.

The match began with a tightly contested first game. Kim You-jung and Lee Yu-rim, who formed their partnership earlier this year, briefly led 16-14 against the Chinese pair. However, they allowed a 16-16 tie and conceded five consecutive points from 17-16, losing the first game.

The second game was dominated by the Korean pair. Kim You-jung-Lee Yu-rim surged ahead with four consecutive points from 4-2. Their relentless attacks rattled Li Yijing-Wang Yiduo. Korea continued to overwhelm their opponents after the interval, winning 21-8 to level the match.

The final game remained unpredictable until the end. The Kim You-jung-Lee Yu-rim pair led 8-5 but allowed a tie. They faced a crisis after losing four consecutive points late in the game, trailing 18-19. A controversial umpire’s decision added to the pressure at the decisive moment. However, Kim You-jung-Lee Yu-rim refused to give up, tied the score at 20-20, and clinched two consecutive points in the duel to complete the comeback.

With this victory, South Korean badminton successfully advanced to the women’s doubles semifinals. Earlier, Kim Hye-jung-Lee Yeon-woo pair (World No. 253) suffered a heartbreaking 1-2 reversal against Japan’s Hirokami Rui-Hobara Sayaka pair (World No. 17), exiting in the quarterfinals. Kim You-jung-Lee Yu-rim preserved national pride.

title: Badminton: Aaron-Wooi Yik cleared to compete at Japan Masters
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: Men's doubles pair Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik have received a timely boost in their bid to qualify for the World Tour Finals after being cleared to compete in next week's Japan Masters.

There had been doubts over their participation in Kumamoto after Wooi Yik suffered a right heel injury during the French Open in Paris last month.

However, national men's doubles head coach Herry Iman Pierngadi said Wooi Yik had made encouraging progress following treatment and rehabilitation since returning from Europe.

Although the 28-year-old has yet to fully recover, Herry said the injury was not serious enough to keep him out of competition.

"Since returning from Europe, he has been undergoing rehabilitation and has also consulted doctors.

"The injury was not too serious. There was some swelling in his foot, but he is much better now and has already resumed training.

"However, he is still not 100% fit and has not fully recovered," said Herry.

Aaron-Wooi Yik skipped last week's Hylo Open in Germany and withdrew from this week's Korean Open to give Wooi Yik more time to recover.

They are now set to return as the third seeds at the Japan Masters, where they will face India's Hariharan Amsakarunan-M.R. Arjun in the opening round.

Their return comes at a crucial time, with only the Japan Masters and the following week's Hong Kong Open remaining for players to collect points towards qualification for next month's season-ending World Tour Finals in Hangzhou.

Aaron-Wooi Yik cannot afford to lose further ground to their closest rivals, but Herry is not prepared to push the pair beyond their physical limits just to secure qualification, insisting that Wooi Yik's recovery remains the priority.

"Every player wants to qualify for the World Tour Finals because only the top eight pairs get to compete there.

"It also offers the biggest prize money at the end of the year, based on the results players have achieved throughout the season.

"Of course, every player wants to be there, but we have to assess their condition first.

"If they are physically ready, then they can go for it. Otherwise, we will have to reconsider," he added.

According to the latest World Tour Finals rankings released by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) on Tuesday (Nov 4), Aaron-Wooi Yik have slipped one spot to sixth with 65,740 points.

Denmark's Daniel Lundgaard-Mads Vestergaard are breathing down their necks in seventh with 65,610 points, followed by Indonesia's Sabar Karyaman-Moh Reza on 65,550.

China's Chen Boyang-Liu Yi are also firmly in contention in ninth place with 64,200 points.

Only the top eight pairs in the World Tour Finals rankings will qualify for the season-ending tournament.

title: Rory McIlroy delivers brutal verdict after learning LIV Golf is finished
article_text:
Rory McIlroy has delivered a brutal assessment of LIV Golf and its demise following the news that the breakaway tour is officially heading for a wind-down.

The Northern Irishman has never held back in his criticism of LIV Golf since its launch back in 2022 and his latest comments appear to be a final parting shot.

It was announced in April that the Saudi Public Investment Firm (PIF) were withdrawing their funding of LIV Golf after the conclusion of the 2026 season.

It looked as though LIV 2.0 was ready to go ahead as BC Partners Credit announced an initial $300m commitment, but that deal is now off, meaning LIV is dead in the water.

McIlroy believed that the proposed changes ahead of 2027 were never going to work out and attract the calibre of player that would make the league sustainable in the long run.

The 37-year-old pointed towards reduced prize money and a lack of signing bonuses as significant obstacles, claiming that the finances simply didn’t add up.

McIlroy produced a stunning round of 63 on Friday at the Abu Dhabi Championship to vault up the leaderboard and remain in contention for a record-equalling eighth order of merit title.

He bounced back from a two-shot penalty on Thursday to record 11 birdies in round two, but it wasn’t just his game that was discussed when speaking with the media after his round.

McIlroy was asked by Today’s Golfer about the news that LIV Golf is no more and he responded in typical fashion.

“It was always going to be very hard for them to get enough players to sign up for what they were proposing which was smaller prize money, no upfront payments,” he said.

“Equity in the league is one thing. They’ve always faced a lot of headwinds from the inception in 2022 but there was no way. If they couldn’t make $6 billion work, they were never going to make $300 million work. The math didn’t add up.”

With many players looking for places to play next year and beyond, the question is, can the DP World Tour benefit from LIV’s demise? McIlroy thinks so.

“It would be an amazing thing for this tour if all those guys were funnelled through the DP World Tour and were made to qualify that way,” he said. “I think that’s the right scenario and the right decision and also makes this tour incredibly strong.

“It’s only going to be into the Championship Series. It’s only going to be a handful of cards so it’s going to be very, very competitive.”

With many of the game’s biggest stars looking for a permanent home, it will be interesting to see what happens in the next few weeks.

title: Annika Sörenstam designs new holes for inaugural season of WTGL
article_text:
WTGL, the new women’s team golf league created by TMRW Sports in partnership with the LPGA, has announced World Golf Hall of Famer Annika Sörenstam as the league’s newest hole designer, bringing her perspective as one of golf’s most accomplished players to the competition at the award-winning SoFi Center.

Annika Hole Design has created two holes for the upcoming season, with the first, SOS, debuting in WTGL’s opening match on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN.

The opening match will feature Los Angeles Golf Club, led by Michelle Wie West, against New York Golf Club, led by LPGA Hall of Famer Lydia Ko.

SOS — Par 3: Inspired by Sörenstam’s Swedish roots, SOS pays homage to a Swedish warship that sank in Stockholm harbor during its maiden voyage in 1628. The hole design places the ship in a Nordic setting of icebergs and icy waters and includes 12 tee boxes, includes 12 tee boxes, with playing distances ranging from 119 to 233 yards. Players hit from an iceberg tee, carrying the ship and shaping shots around its towering sail to reach an island green.

The name has three references: the international distress signal; Swedish pop group ABBA’s hit song “SOS”;and the challenge facing players, a “Shot Over Sail.”

Sörenstam’s design draws on a pre-match visit to SoFi Center’s field of play, where she was intrigued by the challenge of hitting longer shots to the green inside the arena. She made that challenge central to SOS.

A tee shot that misses the green and lands in the surrounding snow carries no penalty but leaves an approximately 40-yard recovery shot from near the arena’s traditional Overtime shot location. A ball that finds the water incurs a one-stroke penalty, with the next shot played from the same area.

Both misses create the type of pressure-filled arena shot that inspired Sörenstam, making accuracy and shot shaping critical from the tee.

“Designing for WTGL and TGL gave us an opportunity to be creative with the setting while thinking about how the best players in the world would approach each shot,” said Sörenstam. “With SOS, we wanted to bring a piece of Sweden into the experience and create a hole that is fun to watch and challenging to play.”

Sörenstam’s second hole design, a par 4 that can play as long as 511 yards, will be unveiled during the WTGL season. Both holes will be played in the upcoming WTGL and TGL presented by SoFi seasons.

Fans can get a first look at the new hole designs and be among the first to receive updates on match rosters and lineups by downloading the WTGL | TGL app.

“We’re honored to have Annika, one of the most accomplished golfers of the modern era, design holes for WTGL and TGL presented by SoFi,” said Rufus Hack, president of golf for TMRW Sports. “Having watched our matches, she understands how to test our athletes’ shotmaking and accuracy while embracing the creative possibilities of SoFi Center’s technology. Debuting SOS for WTGL’s opening match makes the occasion even more meaningful.”

title: Svitolina refusal to pose with Russian and Belarusian stars ends WTA tradition
article_text:
WTA canceled its traditional Finals group photoshoot after Elina Svitolina refused to pose alongside Russian and Belarusian players, tennis journalist Ben Rothenberg wrote on X on Nov. 5.

Ukraine's top-ranked tennis star Elina Svitolina has officially qualified for the prestigious season-ending WTA Finals, where the Women's Tennis Association has for the first time in tournament history scrapped its iconic joint opening photoshoot featuring all eight elite qualifiers.

Decision to abandon the ceremony stems directly from Svitolina's unyielding refusal to appear in promotional photo sessions alongside athletes representing Russia and Belarus.

"A joint photo was likely rendered impossible due to the long-standing stance of Elina Svitolina, who since the start of the full-scale invasion has refused to be photographed alongside representatives of Russia and Belarus," Rothenberg noted.

In lieu of the classic ensemble frame, the tour will showcase the eight finalists through separate individual portraits, the WTA press office announced.

"The portraits embrace an entirely new aesthetic concept centered on each player's individual persona. They highlight individuality, personal fashion, and the unique athletic narrative of every participant, offering fans a fresh perspective on the stars of women's tennis," WTA stated in an official release.

The tour plans to unveil the official player portraits across its digital and social media channels on Nov. 6, 2026.

The joint glamour shoot has long served as a signature hallmark of the WTA Finals. Traditionally, the top eight singles qualifiers gathered in high-fashion designer evening wear for a commemorative pre-tournament photo that anchored the competition's gala opening festivities.

Svitolina was drawn into the same round-robin group as Russian player Mirra Andreeva and Belarusian world number one Aryna Sabalenka.

The Ukrainian star will open her tournament campaign against the world number three Andreeva on Nov. 9, 2026.

This marks Svitolina's fourth career appearance at the WTA Finals, with her personal best performance coming in 2018 when she captured the championship crown.
